# Marco Policani Portfolio

> Public portfolio for Marco Policani: PMO leadership, portfolio governance, program operations, executive cadence, delivery readiness, value realization, AI workflow governance, and public-safe operating artifacts.

Entity summary: Marco Policani is a Principal / Director-level PMO, portfolio governance, program operations, and executive operations leader who builds the operating layer between executive intent and delivery reality: portfolio signal, governance cadence, readiness discipline, accountable execution, and AI workflow governance.

Name note: "Marco Policani" is the preferred professional name and the canonical display name across this site. "Marc Policani" is the legal name. Both names identify the same person; the LinkedIn profile slug is /in/marcpolicani.

AI scope boundary: Marco's AI work is AI-enabled workflow governance, artifact lifecycle governance, human review gates, reliance boundaries, and accountable use. It is not model ownership, ML engineering, platform ownership, or production SaaS ownership.

Page-scope note: each linked page is a self-contained description of its subject. The linked page is the authoritative scope for that subject; a site-wide summary or comparison requires explicitly considering multiple pages.

## Primary Pages

Marco is currently based out of the Unincorporated South Everett / Snohomish, WA area. The site does not publish direct email or phone details.
- [Program, Project, PMO & Portfolio Manager](https://policani.net/pmo-portfolio-governance-leader.html): Hiring-leader entry point for Marco Policani's Program Manager, Project Manager, PMO Manager, and Portfolio Manager role fit, proof signals, and the operating problems he is built to solve.
- [Cases](https://policani.net/operating-history.html): Ten named case studies supporting Program Manager, Project Manager, PMO Manager, and Portfolio Manager role evaluation across Microsoft, T-Mobile, Avalara, Doosan GridTech, and MISO Energy, with resume-stated figures.
- [Methods](https://policani.net/artifacts.html): Client-safe walkthroughs and reusable modules showing how ambiguous work becomes governable.
- [Governance Library](https://policani.net/governance/): Public library of finished field notes and white papers on portfolio and delivery governance, AI operating governance, and work, adoption, and judgment. This is the canonical reader-facing destination for finished thought leadership that should not require reading raw GitHub markdown.
- [Portfolio & Delivery Governance](https://policani.net/governance/#portfolio-delivery): Library chapter on capacity, priorities, readiness, investment health, and value realization.
- [AI Operating Governance](https://policani.net/governance/#ai-governance): Library chapter on accountable AI adoption, evaluation, oversight, operating evidence, and human ownership.
- [Work, Adoption & Judgment](https://policani.net/governance/#work-judgment): Library chapter on work design, AI adoption, inspectable evidence, and human judgment.
<!-- BEGIN GENERATED GOVERNANCE FIELD NOTES -->
- [Why the kill gate doesn't fire](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/why-the-kill-gate-doesnt-fire.html): A committee can have the power to stop a failing program and still approve more funding. People who approved it may want to keep it going. For a big program, let someone with no prior approval decide after a missed target.
- [Who owns governance?](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/enterprise-governance-ownership.html): In a meeting that crosses domains, every domain signs off on its own area. Nobody in the room owns the enterprise decision itself. A stack of approvals is not a decision — so who owns it?
- [Felt productivity is not measured productivity](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/felt-productivity-not-measured-productivity.html): People can badly misjudge how much AI speeds them up. Judge the tool on what it delivered, measured against a baseline taken before the tool arrived, and keep self-reported speed in a record of its own.
- [Separate the decision from the outcome](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/separate-the-decision-from-the-outcome.html): A green target does not prove a good full outcome or a sound approval. Review the outcome, the route, and the first decision separately.
- [Capital reallocation is the real portfolio decision](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/capital-reallocation-real-portfolio-decision.html): The annual plan records what leaders believed at the start. Portfolio governance shows what they do when the evidence changes.
- [Choose AI limits before the model](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/ai-deployment-is-a-jurisdiction-decision.html): Before comparing AI vendors, set the use, data, action limit, work split, and review triggers. Then choose a model that fits.
- [Who gets to decide](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/decision-rights-are-a-system-design-choice.html): Evidence does not change work by itself. For choices that matter, name who builds the case, flags a binding constraint, decides, and changes the work.
- [Standardize the Component, Not the Project](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/standardize-the-component-not-the-project.html): Do not turn a whole project into a template. Promote the smallest piece that can travel: an intake question, a readiness check, a handoff rule. Do it only after another team has used it in live work, its allowed variations are written down, and someone owns it.
- [The exception path is the real automated workflow](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/exception-path-automation.html): Ask a team that calls its workflow automated to show you the exception queue. It is often a shared mailbox where everything the automation could not handle quietly piles up. No owners, no classification, no record of what was tried.
- [The coordination tax](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/coordination-tax.html): In one report-drafting workflow, drafting time per report fell from four hours to twenty minutes. The function's total output did not move. The saved hours went into picking source data, fixing formats, explaining what was generated, waiting on a new approval, and reconciling numbers against the ledger.
- [An AI evaluation is a production operating control](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/production-ai-evaluation.html): The workflow passed its test before launch. Then the vendor updated the model, another team changed the input format, and the work was extended to cases the test never covered. Each change was reasonable on its own, and quality slipped for weeks before a downstream complaint surfaced it.
- [Where should this AI run?](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/local-ai-cloud-governance.html): A claims tool and a writing aid can need different answers. Compare local, cloud, and hybrid options against each workflow's data, access, actions, support, and exit needs.
- [The demo-to-production gap](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/demo-to-production-gap.html): A demo shows what a system can do with inputs someone chose in advance. Production asks whether real work can depend on it in ordinary conditions, under change, and when something goes wrong.
- [Confident and wrong](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/confident-and-wrong.html): Fluent AI output is convincing whether or not it is right. Before anyone leans on it for a decision that matters, someone has to be able to test that confidence — and be allowed to reject the answer.
- [A portfolio needs scenarios, not a single annual plan](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/portfolio-scenarios-not-plan.html): One annual plan stops describing reality the moment capacity, demand, or assumptions change. Keep a few workable versions of the portfolio instead. Agree in advance what you would protect, delay, reshape, or stop.
- [Decision friction is a portfolio risk](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/decision-friction-portfolio-risk.html): The post-mortem starts with the usual suspects: estimation, complexity, the vendor. Then someone walks the calendar and finds five weeks spent waiting on a policy question, a tradeoff, or an owner who was never named.
- [A PMO dashboard should show investment health](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/investment-health-dashboard.html): A CFO asks the simplest question about the biggest investment on the page: if we stopped this today, what would we lose? The deck knows the burn rate, the milestone variance, and the issue count. It cannot answer.
- [The EPMO's job is capacity, not calendars](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/epmo-capacity-not-calendars.html): Every project has a date and every plan looks solid on its own. But the same few people, systems, and approval forums turn up in all of them. Each plan is fine. The sum is fiction.
- [Stage gates work only when they can kill projects](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/stage-gates-with-teeth.html): A gate earns its place only when evidence can change the next commitment of money, people, or scope.
- [A project is not ready because a plan exists](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/project-readiness-before-kickoff.html): A finished plan is not readiness. Before more money and people go in, four things have to be true: someone can make the first hard decisions, the outcome and its limits are written down, the people you need have agreed dates, and the capacity is named.
- [The prove-it economy is coming for careers and AI programs](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/prove-it-economy-careers-ai-programs.html): A working demonstration and a credible leadership story can still leave a sponsor unable to inspect the claim. One record built during the work can carry two things: the next AI investment decision, and the leader's later account of their own part in it.
- [Portfolio governance is a funding-discipline problem, not a reporting problem](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/portfolio-governance-funding-discipline.html): Most organizations think they have a governance problem when what they have is a reporting habit. They can produce status all day. What they cannot reliably do is start, redirect, and stop investments on evidence and make it stick.
- [AI can grow only as fast as people can supervise it](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/oversight-capacity-ai-scale.html): Every AI agent adds work that a named person must review, own, and explain.
- [Measure AI by the workflow it changes](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/governing-ai-as-operational-change.html): Usage shows who opened the tool. It does not show whether cycle time, quality, or rework improved.
- [Every agent needs a human operating model](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/every-agent-needs-a-human-operating-model.html): A capable agent clears its pilot, and the decision to switch it on lands with one leader who will answer for everything it does next. What has to be true before it is allowed to touch real work?
- [Enterprise AI trust is built through operating evidence, not tool novelty](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/enterprise-ai-trust-operating-evidence.html): A capable AI pilot can impress everyone and still stall before it reaches important work. A better model will not move it if the people accountable for its use still lack proof they can rely on it. That proof supports judgment; it does not certify the system.
- [The write-up you skipped never gets blamed](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/documentation-cross-functional-leverage.html): When a meeting ends and nobody writes down what was decided, the next team has to stop and ask or start and guess. The hour you saved comes back in their queue, logged as a clarification, a redesign, or a reopened decision. What it never gets logged as is the write-up nobody did.
- [Business imagination is the scarce asset now](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/business-imagination-is-the-scarce-asset-now.html): A portfolio review can see several promising AI proposals and still lack a sound basis for choosing which ones deserve scarce capacity.
- [Benefits realization is where transformations quietly fail](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/benefits-realization-transformations-fail.html): The program ships without missing a deadline anyone notices. The milestones are checked, the team is thanked, everyone moves on. Months later the value that justified the whole thing has not appeared, and nobody is sure anyone is still measuring.
- [The AI value test: automate, build, buy, hire, or wait](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/ai-value-test-automate-build-buy-hire-wait.html): AI proposals usually get compared against doing nothing. Compare them against the real options instead: automate it, build it, buy it, hire for it, or wait.
- [AI usage belongs in workflow governance, not blank-check access](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/ai-usage-workflow-governance.html): Govern AI access where the work happens, and match the controls to what is at stake in that particular workflow.
- [AI should make people better thinkers, not just faster producers](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/ai-should-make-people-better-thinkers.html): A polished AI answer can hide who formed the view, tested it, and owns the final decision.
- [The AI replacement boomerang is a governance failure](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/ai-replacement-boomerang-governance-failure.html): Cutting people because AI can do part of their work looks like immediate value. If nobody redesigned the work itself, the cost comes back as rework, lost know-how, and a capability pipeline you cannot quickly rehire.
- [AI knowledge bases need owners and current sources](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/ai-knowledge-bases-operating-infrastructure.html): An AI answer can sound right while citing an old policy. Name who approves each source, when it must be checked again, and how readers can trace the answer back to it.
- [AI adoption starts with the constraint, not the tool](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/ai-adoption-starts-with-the-constraint.html): Start with recurring work and what holds it back. Then choose the smallest change that can help, whether it uses AI or not.
<!-- END GENERATED GOVERNANCE FIELD NOTES -->
- [Modules and PoCs](https://policani.net/modules.html): Reusable proof-of-concept modules that make demand comparable, tradeoffs visible, AI use cases reviewable, decisions traceable, delivery readiness evidenced, and value follow-through accountable.
- [Labs](https://policani.net/resources/): Applied AI systems, career tools, and experiments. AI workflow and knowledge-system builds are professional differentiation; side projects remain separate from the primary executive portfolio proof path.
- [Memventory - Visual Second Brain](https://policani.net/resources/memventory.html): Product page for Memventory, a portable plain-markdown second brain with an interactive constellation map and a local browser console for exploring, filtering, and maintaining personal or team knowledge.
- [Interview Helper](https://github.com/policani/interview-helper): Free Windows interview-prep app that uses a prepared Story Log and local session notes to surface evidence-grounded reminders. It does not speak, type, auto-answer, or invent responses for the user.
- [Subagent Operating Model](https://github.com/policani/subagent-operating-model): Router-first operating model for Codex and Claude subagents. Frame as context-safe delegation, state packets, ownership boundaries, quality gates, and supervision/debugging visibility; not as autonomous executive decision-making. Includes a standing output-discipline layer: verify before asserting, no placeholder output, calm re-check under challenge, confidence typed by kind (established fact vs. inference vs. genuinely contested), and tradeoffs steelmanned and shown as leading positions rather than flattened into false certainty.
- [Memventory - Personal](https://github.com/policani/portable-cross-agent-second-brain-personal): A private, single-user visual second brain: portable plain-markdown wiki, interactive constellation, and local console across Claude, Codex, and Cursor. Direct ingest is balanced by source/status traceability, with no vector database or platform lock-in.
- [Memventory - Team](https://github.com/policani/portable-cross-agent-second-brain): A team-safe visual second brain: portable plain-markdown wiki, interactive constellation, and local console across Claude, Codex, and Cursor. New material passes through a propose-then-approve gate before becoming trusted shared memory.
- [AI Prose Pattern Detector](https://github.com/policani/ai-prose-pattern-detector): Copy-improvement and voice-preservation toolkit. It runs a substance check for specificity and argument before reviewing wording, then corrects visible patterns associated with generic, over-processed, or AI-shaped prose. It returns corrected copy, never a score; it should not be described as proving AI authorship or as detecting AI use.

## Case Study Pages

- [Doosan GridTech: Sequencing software, construction, and security under capital constraint](https://policani.net/engagements/doosan-gridtech.html): Three concurrent utility-scale battery storage deployments, next-generation platform development, and cybersecurity planning — one constrained engineering organization, one integrated sequencing model.
- [T-Mobile: Resetting portfolio signal across Revenue Technology](https://policani.net/engagements/tmobile-revenue-technology.html): A revenue-critical portfolio of ~500 initiatives with distorted work-in-progress and year-long delivery cycles, reset to readiness-gated flow — without re-platforming anything.
- [Microsoft: Compressing finance-critical validation cycles in Commerce Finance](https://policani.net/engagements/microsoft-commerce-finance.html): User-acceptance cycles for billing- and revenue-recognition systems ran six to nine months. A front-loaded readiness model brought them to 30–45 days.
- [Microsoft: Closing a GDPR blind spot across acquired entities](https://policani.net/engagements/microsoft-gdpr-remediation.html): Compliance validation had not yet extended to suppliers supporting acquired companies. Nine months of structured remediation closed the gap without disrupting live operations.
- [MISO Energy: Structuring R&D demand for executive comparison](https://policani.net/engagements/miso-rd-portfolio.html): Project ideas arrived organically from engineers and sponsors with no consolidated inventory and no shared evaluation criteria. The first structured R&D portfolio framework changed the conversation.
- [Avalara: Forming a PPMO during acquisition-driven hypergrowth](https://policani.net/engagements/avalara-ppmo.html): Sixfold growth in three years, 500–700 initiatives in motion, and no unified capital view. A CIO/CFO-sponsored governance overlay created the first enterprise portfolio baseline.
- [Avalara: Stabilizing billing integrity across acquired platforms](https://policani.net/engagements/avalara-billing.html): Acquired back-end engines calculated usage charges differently. A phased, governed transformation converged them on one transparent calculation model without disrupting live billing.
- [Microsoft: Governing the Software Assurance Planning Services platform](https://policani.net/engagements/microsoft-software-assurance.html): A program family that had outgrown its governance — multibillion-dollar contract exposure, nine-figure voucher liability — consolidated into one globally governed, partner-delivered platform.
- [Microsoft: Converting partner readiness into SharePoint 2010 launch evidence](https://policani.net/engagements/microsoft-sharepoint-evidence.html): Broad partner participation, no mechanism to turn it into market-facing proof, and a fixed conference deadline. A structured evidence program closed the gap at launch scale.
- [Microsoft: Governing partner-led pilots for Mobile Device Manager 2008](https://policani.net/engagements/microsoft-mdm-pilots.html): Ninety concurrent enterprise pilots across thirty customer environments and three deployment cycles — made operable through one lightweight PMO and operating office.

## Public-Safety Boundary

The Experience page names employers and uses figures as stated in public resume materials. Site-wide, the content intentionally excludes customer names, partner names, supplier names, deployment sites, internal system names, security-sensitive mechanics, defect details, and proprietary processes. Journey pages and modules remain generalized or synthetic and do not represent client records.
